items.h: Fantasy football buzz: Starters on bye? Finish your lineup with these streamers
items.s: Streaming picks for your Week 8 lineup at quarterback, running back, wide receiver and tight end.

items.h: Could Keenan Allen Be the Next Colts Player on the Move?
items.s: The Indianapolis Colts made headlines by trading six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday, and NFL Insider Ari Meirov believes more moves could be on the way, specifically listing wide receiver Keenan Allen among a group of players on whom the Colts could be willing to listen to offers. Playing for his third team in as many seasons, the 14-year veteran leads the Colts with 44 targets, which he has converted into 29 receptions, 258 yards, and a touchdown. Well beyond his early-career durability concerns, Allen has been a fantasy producer almost everywhere he's gone, finishing as a WR3 or better in eight of the past nine seasons, and a move to a more…

items.h: Three catches in loss
items.s: Allen caught all three of his targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings. Allen was held to his fewest catches, receiving yards and targets since Week 2 as the Colts struggled to establish a passing attack against Minnesota's impressive defense. The wide receiver still led the team in all three categories, and he'll have a chance for better production in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

items.h: Keenan Allen has More Waiver-Wire Appeal With Teammate Injured
items.s: Indianapolis Colts veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen certainly does not have the kind of fantasy ceiling that he used to have in his prime, but he has become a more intriguing WR4/flex in deeper leagues with tight end Tyler Warren (groin) missing the last two games. Allen played just over half of the Colts' offensive snaps in Sunday's Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings and caught just three passes (three targets), but he led the team with 31 receiving yards (10.3 yards per catch). In last week's loss to the division-rival Tennessee Titans, the 34-year-old caught a season-high eight passes on 11 targets for 82 yards (10.3 yards per reception). With Josh Downs struggling and Alec Pierce…

items.h: Keenan Allen hauls in three passes Sunday
items.s: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts 16-10 loss against the Vikings. It was a low-volume passing day for the Colts offense as Allen led the team in receiving. He remains a low upside WR3/flex play for fantasy managers.

items.h: Keenan Allen a Solid Wide Receiver Streamer Option in Week 7
items.s: Across five games so far in 2026, Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has recorded 26 catches for 227 yards and a touchdown on 40 targets. While the 34-year-old is only averaging 8.7 yards per reception, he's currently seeing eight targets per game. In Week 7, Allen and the Colts will face the fearsome Minnesota Vikings defense. With his ability to win in the short and intermediate areas, Allen could continue his role as the security blanket for Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. Additionally, Indianapolis will be without tight end Tyler Warren (groin) for the second straight week. With Warren sidelined in Week 6, Allen logged eight catches for 82 yards on 11 targets. In leagues…

items.h: Keenan Allen Hard to Trust in Week 7
items.s: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen scored 16.2 PPR fantasy points in Week 6 as the clear No. 1 pass-catcher for his team, but he should probably be benched in Week 7 in anticipation of the toughest defensive test (by far) his team will face this season. The Colts will head northwest to face the vicious Minnesota Vikings defense. They've allowed just 27.1 PPR fantasy points to opposing wideouts this season, and their blitz-heavy scheme has wrecked opposing offensive game plans all season. Additionally, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has been unproductive this year and has turned the ball over nine times while scoring just five total touchdowns. Allen would normally be a nice…

items.h: Keenan Allen (rest) returns to practice Thursday
items.s: Keenan Allen (rest) returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday. As expected, Allen was back at practice on Thursday after getting the day off on Wednesday. He was a full participant and should be fully good to go for Week 7's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

items.h: Fantasy football: Six surging players to believe in
items.s: Six fantasy football players whose production is surging and why you can expect it to continue.

items.h: Keenan Allen (rest) sidelined at practice Wednesday
items.s: Keenan Allen (rest) was sidelined at Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday. The veteran was held out of Wednesday's practice, which was to be expected, since the Colts have made a habit out of giving him at least one day off per week. He should be good to go for Week 7.

items.h: Keenan Allen's Steady Target Volume Boosts Waiver Appeal
items.s: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen is getting enough work to matter in PPR leagues, even without a touchdown every week. His 11 targets in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans were a season high, and he turned them into eight catches for 82 yards, also season bests. Over his past three appearances, Allen has 19 receptions for 190 yards and a touchdown on 29 targets, and he's seen at least nine targets each time. That makes the 34-year-old a worthwhile pickup in 10-team PPR leagues and deeper, with high-end WR4 value and the potential for WR2/WR3 finishes when the volume turns into production. Tight end Tyler Warren (groin) was inactive Sunday, which opened up more…

items.h: Keenan Allen grabs eight passes in loss to Titans
items.s: Keenan Allen caught 8 of 11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. Allen led the Colts in targets, receptions, and yards in the upset loss. It's a vintage performance for Allen, but if Tyler Warren, who missed this game, is back for Week 7, it will likely signal a downturn in volume for the veteran. However, even so, he's been usable each of the last three weeks, and that trend will likely continue.

items.h: Allen caught eight of 11 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Titans.
items.s: With tight end Tyler Warren (groin) inactive, Allen became the preferred option for Daniel Jones when he needed to move the chains, and the veteran wideout led the Colts in catches, targets and receiving yards while setting personal season highs in all three categories. Mo Alie-Cox was on the other end of Jones' only TD pass, however. Allen will take a 26-227-1 line on 40 targets into a Week 7 clash with the Vikings.

items.s: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.h: Allen was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice due to rest.
items.s: Allen previously missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin issue and was listed with the same injury on the team's Week 5 report, but his absence from practice to begin Week 6 looks to be a planned off day. In his return from a one-game absence during this past Sunday's 34-22 loss to the Steelers, Allen logged just 32 of the Colts' 71 offensive snaps, but he could see an uptick in playing time this weekend against the Titans now that he's further removed from the groin injury.

items.h: Allen (groin) isn't practicing Wednesday, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.s: Allen sat out the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin issue, but he was cleared to play in this past Sunday's 34-22 loss to the Steelers after practicing in a limited fashion Wednesday and Thursday before practicing fully Friday. Though he's off the field to begin Week 6 prep, Allen isn't necessarily dealing with a setback coming out of the loss to Pittsburgh and may just be getting a maintenance day. Allen played less than half of the Colts' offensive snaps in his return to action in Week 5, but so long as he resumes practicing by the end of the week, he'll likely be ready…

items.h: Allen caught five of nine targets for 45 yards in Sunday's Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh.
items.s: Allen missed Week 4 due to a groin injury but was able to return to action Sunday. His nine targets tied for the top mark on the Colts, and his five receptions were second behind tight end Tyler Warren. Allen has been relatively consistent this season with at least five catches in three of his four contests, but he's averaging a meager 8.1 yards per reception, which is on pace for a career low.

items.h: Allen (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 5 game against the Steelers.
items.s: The veteran receiver had entered the weekend with optimism surrounding his status for Sunday's game after getting a full practice in Friday, and Allen's availability is now official. Before sitting out Indianapolis' Week 4 victory over the Commanders in London, Allen put together the most productive performance of his brief Colts tenure, posting a 6-63-1 line on nine targets during a Week 3 win over the Texans. In his return Sunday against Pittsburgh, Allen is expected to slide back into his usual No. 2 receiver role alongside Josh Downs.

items.h: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
items.s: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.h: Allen (groin) is expected to play Sunday against the Steelers, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
items.s: A full practice Friday was promising for Allen's prospects of suiting up against the Steelers, and it appears he will be able to give it a go. His status for Week 5 will officially be revealed when the Colts release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.h: Allen (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.s: After back-to-back limited sessions earlier in the week, Allen got in a full practice Friday. However, he still hasn't gotten the full green light for Sunday's contest. If he plays, the veteran wideout will slide back into a prominent role alongside Josh Downs, bumping Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin back down the depth chart.

items.h: Allen (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.s: It was another limited session for Allen, who is working his way back from a groin injury that kept him out against the Commanders in Week 4. Allen is trending toward being ready to go against the Steelers on Sunday, which would give the Colts' receiving corps a much-needed boost.

items.h: Allen (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: After missing last Sunday's win over the Commanders, Allen's return to the practice field puts him on track to suit up Sunday against the Steelers. He should slot back into full-time duties alongside Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell, with Ashton Dulin heading back to more of a special-teams role.

items.h: Allen (groin) will practice Wednesday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
items.s: After sitting out the Week 4 loss to the Commanders in London, Allen's ability to practice in some fashion to begin Week 5 prep puts him on a good track to play this Sunday against the Steelers. With Alec Pierce (heel) still on injured reserve, the Colts need all the help they can get at receiver after Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin (hamstring) were forced into heavy snaps alongside Josh Downs in Week 4.

items.h: Fantasy football Week 4 inactives: Coker ruled out for Sunday Night Football
items.s: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.h: Allen (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against Washington.
items.s: After entering the weekend with a questionable tag following a non-participant listing Friday, Allen will now miss Sunday's contest in London. Without Allen or Alec Pierce (heel), Josh Downs will be the Colts' top receiver for Week 4, with Darius Slayton, Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Deion Burks and tight end Tyler Warren all in line for more targets. Allen's next chance to take the field is Week 5 against the Steelers on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.h: Allen (groin) was listed as a non-participant for Friday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.s: After logging a limited practice Thursday, Allen moved the wrong direction Friday with a DNP tag and now carries a questionable designation into Sunday's contest in London. That leaves the Colts' veteran wide receiver with some added uncertainty for Week 4 availability. If Allen is unable to go, the Colts will dip even deeper into their wideout depth with Alec Pierce (heel, IR) already on the shelf for multiple weeks. Josh Downs and Tyler Warren would be in line to soak up most of the targets.

items.h: Allen was a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to a groin injury.
items.s: The veteran receiver was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice due to rest, but an injury played a part in his restrictions a day later. With that in mind, Allen may need to turn in a full practice Friday to approach Sunday's game against the Commanders in London without an injury designation. Allen is coming off his best performance of the season in Week 3, when he turned in a 6-63-1 receiving line on nine targets in a 19-17 win over the Texans.

items.h: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Gordon leads options to replace Achane for Week 4 and beyond
items.s: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.h: Allen caught six of nine targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
items.s: Allen was able to take advantage of the absence of Alec Pierce (heel) in Week 3, matching his season-high six receptions while notching his first touchdown of the year in the second quarter on a six-yard pass from Daniel Jones. With Pierce set to miss extended time, Allen will have a chance to carve out a significant role for himself as a reliable option for Indianapolis.

items.h: Allen caught one of five targets for five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
items.s: Allen failed to capitalize on the first-half exit of fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel). Dating back to last season with the Chargers, the 34-year-old Allen is mired in a 12-game regular-season touchdown drought, during which he has exceeded 44 receiving yards only once. Snapping that funk won't be easy in Week 3 against the Texans.

items.h: Allen "is facing a minimum three-game suspension" in connection with his August arrest, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Allen was formally charged with two misdemeanors last week after being arrested on DUI charges in late August, and the NFL could levy a suspension of three games or more for his actions. Per the report, "Allen is not expected to miss playing time while the case proceeds through the courts."

items.h: Allen has been formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his August arrest, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
items.s: Allen was arrested in late August, and he has officially been charged with two counts, including "OVWI with a BAC of .15 or more." Per the same source, "The NFL's policy says an eight-game suspension could be levied with aggravating circumstances (including 'extreme intoxication' with a BAC of .15 or more)."

items.h: Allen caught all six of his targets for 32 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
items.s: Allen played 36 of 54 offensive snaps against Baltimore and ran 26 routes on Daniel Jones' 34 dropbacks. He ran six fewer routes than Josh Downs, but Allen's microscopic 3.7-yard average depth of target made him an easy pitch-and-catch option for the quarterback. Allen lacks explosiveness at this stage of his career, but he's always been able to earn targets. He's a low-floor fantasy option at 34 years old.

items.h: Colts general manager Chris Ballard said Tuesday that Allen will play in Week 1 against the Ravens, Jake Arthur of Colts Roundtable reports.
items.s: Allen will not face discipline from the team following his arrest on DUI charges Sunday. "We should be good," said Ballard when asked about that on Tuesday, and added that "Good people make mistakes. [Allen] is a tremendous human being...he'll work through the process of the legal system." It appears that Allen can now shift his focus to getting up to speed with the team in advance of the season-opener on Sept. 13 against the Ravens.

items.h: Allen was arrested early Sunday morning and charged with DUI, FOX59 reports.
items.s: Per the report, Allen was arrested overnight in Indianapolis "on preliminary charges of (DWI) and DWI endangering a person." The Colts, via Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan, issued a statement saying, "We are aware of the incident involving Allen last night. We are in the process of gathering more information and have no further comment at this time."

items.h: Allen caught his only target for 24 yards in Saturday's 25-16 preseason loss to the Lions.
items.s: Having just signed with Indianapolis less than two weeks ago, Allen saw his first game action for his new club and quickly produced a big gain on Anthony Richardson's first pass attempt of the afternoon, helping to set up a field goal. Top wideouts Alec Pierce (ankle) and Josh Downs (calf), as well as top tight end Tyler Warren (groin), are all carrying injury designations to close out the preseason, so Allen could end up having a bigger role in the passing attack than expected once Week 1 rolls around. The 34-year-old showed he can still be an effective possession option in 2025 with the…

items.h: Allen will make his first appearance with the Colts in Saturday's preseason finale against the Lions, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Allen began practicing with the Colts a week ago, and he is now set to see action in a game setting for the first time since joining Indianapolis earlier this month. Fellow wideouts Alec Pierce (ankle) and Josh Downs (calf) are both banged up, but both have a chance to take the field in Week 1, so Allen will presumably open the regular season as the third option at the wideout spot for the Colts.

items.h: Allen made his Colts practice debut in Thursday's joint practice with the Falcons, Noah Compton of SI.com reports.
items.s: Allen wasn't expected to participate in team drills after signing earlier this week, but he took four reps in 11-on-11 work against Atlanta's defense. "He's been productive every single year he's been in the league. So obviously, we want him to be productive again this year," coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday. "He'll come in - obviously, he's been in this system. He'll pick it up quickly, but he'll play outside. He'll play inside. We'll move all our guys around." Allen is expected to be a mainstay in three-wide sets for Indianapolis and could even push Josh Downs out of two-wide sets once…

items.h: The Colts are signing Allen to a one-year contract worth up to $8.32 million, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
items.s: Allen is coming off a 2025 return campaign with the Chargers during which he caught 81 of 122 targets for 777 yards and four touchdowns over 17 regular-season games. It was the 34-year-old's ninth straight year with over 700 receiving yards, so he appears to still have gas left in the tank. Allen should give Colts QB Daniel Jones an experienced and reliable weapon in the passing game, and the veteran wideout's addition would take on even more significance if Alec Pierce (ankle), who is currently on the active/PUP list, misses any time at the beginning of the campaign.

items.h: GM Joe Hortiz noted Thursday on the 'Up & Adams' show that the "door is not closed" regarding a possible return to the Chargers by Allen, Eric Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Allen, who caught 81 of his 122 targets for 777 yards and four TD in 17 regular-season games with Los Angeles in 2025, remains unsigned at this stage of the offseason. For now, Hortiz said that the Chargers are "in a spot where we're looking at the roster and letting (the team's) young guys get a chance. But I've had some communication with Keenan's representation and we've talked." As things stand, Tre' Harris, Brenen Thompson, KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Derius Davis are in line to compete for WR targets that don't go to Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston.

items.h: Allen had three receptions on eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 16-3 loss to the Patriots in the wild-card round.
items.s: Allen suffered a disappointing end to his return to the Chargers in 2025 when he finished Sunday's playoff loss with a catch rate below 50 percent. The 33-year-old wasn't on the same page with QB Justin Herbert like they were during the regular season when the duo connected on 66 percent of their attempts, resulting in a 81-777-4 receiving line for the veteran receiver. Allen will become an unrestricted free agent in 2026, so the future Hall of Famer will be in control of his destiny should he decide to return for a 14th season.

items.h: Allen finished with seven receptions on 13 targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Broncos.
items.s: Allen was one of the few starters head coach Jim Harbaugh allowed to suit up for Sunday's regular-season finale against Denver. The 33-year-old Allen responded to last week's one-catch performance by leading his club in targets, receptions and yardage with backup QB Trey Lance under center. Allen produced solid PPR numbers in his return to the Chargers this season, accruing 81 receptions for 777 yards and four touchdowns across 17 games. Look for Allen to serve as a security blanket for QB Justin Herbert against the Patriots in the wild-card round of the playoffs next Sunday.
